text:
Alexa M: Heads-up — I'm proposing a new pricing add-on: "Timebox Surge Buffer". It's a per-hour buffer customers pre-buy each month to guarantee extra throughput for short windows. Idea: banked burst capacity charged as hour-units rather than tokens. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Jon Chen: Love the concept. How does it interact with reserved capacity? e.g., can Dedicated customers buy buffers for cross-region failovers?

Alexa M: Good Q. Plan A: buffers are cross-model, orthogonal to Dedicated reservations. They route to best available pool; fallback prioritized after reserved capacity. Need input from infra on routing + billing.

Ashok Patel: Implementation flag: billing will need hourly consumption metering + rollups. Also need a graceful degradation policy when buffer exhausted. We can surface an `surge_buffer` field in routing decisions.

pricing-bot: sim calc: 10hr buffer on p50 workload ~ +12% monthly cost vs baseline for customer X (est).

Maria Lopez: For launch, propose: pilot with 2 customers (one SaaS, one platform) + success criteria: <5% unserved peak events, <10% cost delta vs current over a month, and clear telemetry in Console.

Jon Chen: UX: Add-on config in Console should be Timebox units (hours) + window size e.g., 1h/4h. Also API sample?

Jon Chen: ```
POST /v1/surge_buffers
{
  "customer_id": "acme-corp",
  "buffer_hours": 10,
  "window": "1h",
  "route_policy": "surge-first"
}
```

Ashok Patel: Dev note: runtime needs token->hour conversion assumptions for varied model latencies. We should do unit testing with gpt-like and quantized 7b variants.

Alexa M: Agree. Next steps: I'll add to roadmap board, tag infra + billing. @Jon Chen can you pick 2 pilot candidates? @Maria Lopez will own launch metrics.

Jon Chen: On it. I have one customer in mind (edu-platform). Will ping them today.

Maria Lopez: I'll draft success metrics and dashboard fields. Quick Q: do we bundle with QoS addon or keep separate? :question:

Alexa M: Keep separate initially; easier to measure. We can bundle later.
